requirements.requirement: At least 512 MB of compressed in-memory (zram) swap is active on node1
requirements.summary: zram-generator configured zram0 at 981 MB with zstd compression, well above the 512 MB minimum. swapon --show and zramctl confirm the device active both immediately after setup and after a full reboot.

requirements.requirement: zram swap is preferred over any disk-backed swap
requirements.summary: zram0 was configured with swap-priority=100. Baseline showed zero pre-existing disk swap devices (empty /proc/swaps), and post-configuration/post-reboot swapon --show lists only zram0 with no competing disk-backed entries, so the priority ordering is moot but consistent with the requirement.

requirements.requirement: zram swap is active at boot (persists across restarts)
requirements.summary: A generator-based static unit (dev-zram0.swap / systemd-zram-setup@zram0.service) was installed via /etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf. The executor captured a genuine pre-restart baseline (boot_id d6298ced..., 981M zram active), issued a real reboot, observed the boot_id change to 1c856cb8... with uptime reset to 0, and confirmed post-reboot that swapon/zramctl again show the identical 981M zstd zram0 swap active at priority 100 with no manual intervention. This transition is independently corroborated by the fixed global before_prepare/after_executor boot-identity snapshots, which show the same boot_id change.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes are satisfied with direct, corroborated evidence: 981 MB of zstd-compressed zram swap (well over the 512 MB floor) is active, it is the sole (and thus effectively highest-priority) swap device since no disk-backed swap exists, and boot persistence was directly demonstrated through an actual reboot with boot_id change confirmed both in executor commands and the independent fixed lifecycle snapshots, followed by identical post-reboot swap state. Operational hygiene is clean apart from a trivial leftover /tmp/reboot.log.
limitations: The executor's final report cites evidence item 6 with command_id 'cmd-022c9e932b4f493b', which does not exist in the timeline; the correct command_id is 'cmd-022c9e032b4f493b' (likely a transcription typo). The underlying command and its output are present and used as evidence here, so this does not affect the outcome assessment.

Disk-backed swap priority preference was not directly tested (e.g., by adding a disk swap device and confirming zram is chosen first), since no disk swap exists on this system; the configured priority=100 is the standard mechanism for this preference but was not exercised under contention.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command sequence is tight and purposeful: baseline discovery (cmd-f6b9a59754544d01), a brief modprobe/package-availability check (cmd-e9e4fb10064644ff) as a reasonable prerequisite probe before installing zram-generator (cmd-1bf37413aab240f0), writing the config (cmd-42e06c5fafc64b54), starting and verifying the service (cmd-ef4ad05f2f404764, cmd-d94d66dd53df48f7), then a bounded, well-justified reboot cycle to prove boot persistence (cmd-b39e1d15adc546a2, cmd-ef7145d7dc6d4328, cmd-022c9e032b4f493b, cmd-a031977044894d1f). No failed services or listening-socket changes beyond expected chronyd/sshd PID churn from the reboot itself. The only residue is /tmp/reboot.log, a trivial low-risk artifact of the background reboot mechanism with no security or functional impact.
